## What

Codex's managed PreCompact bridge can stop with `request_rejected: superuser_invalid_bearer` when a session carries a workspace-scoped `PAPERCUSP_HOME` but its MCP route targets the shared host operator. Workspace state and operator credentials are different boundaries. The hook previously read `papercuspPath('superuser-token')`, which resolved the session's workspace token; the shared operator validates its host token.

## Why it matters

This is an authentication failure before `session:request-compaction` executes. Repeating the same managed carry request does not repair the token source. Native compaction remains stopped intentionally so a refused managed carry does not discard the session's managed state. Existing tests injected `readToken: () => 'secret-token'` and therefore never exercised real file selection.

## How to apply

`precompact-managed-carry.mjs` follows the existing ptool distinction: an explicit `PAPERCUSP_SUPERUSER_TOKEN_PATH` remains authoritative, then `PAPERCUSP_MCP_TOKEN_FILE`; `PAPERCUSP_OPERATOR_HOME` selects the operator's real home; a `PAPERCUSP_HOME` under `.papercusp-workspaces/<workspace>` selects the shared host credential; other isolated `PAPERCUSP_HOME` values retain their own token. Missing explicit or isolated credentials fail closed, without trying another identity. Read the token at hook execution time. Preserve the exact MCP URL, signed role route, and native session carrier.

Diagnose using read-only `coord:whoami` with each candidate credential kept in process memory. A tools/list result from the local MCP proxy alone does not prove that the operator accepts a given token: the proxy can supply its own upstream credential. Never print tokens or signed query strings. Refresh the installed shared hook atomically, with a file lock and installer provenance stamp, so existing sessions use the fix at their next hook invocation.

## Evidence

WI-6554700010050915, 2026-11-17: the same read-only call to the live operator at :3070 rejected the workspace token with `superuser_invalid_bearer` and accepted the host token. The native Vitest suite reproduced eight failures before the fix and passed 39/39 after it, including real-file credential selection for shared and isolated homes, both explicit pins, missing-pin refusal, and continued native-compaction veto on bearer rejection. The first passing local run had moving-HEAD provenance; it demonstrates local behavior and is not a claim about a shipped main build.
